atomicityRationale: One bounded content competence: explain how meiotic chromosomal recombination creates new genetic combinations using supplied correct models. Independent chromosome assortment and corresponding segment exchange are the two biologically distinct contributions to this one explanatory phenomenon, not independent construction, quantitative routines, phase memorization or molecular mechanism skills. A coherent chromosome comparison can assess the whole relation.
interpretationLimit: The original NI bullet names principles without enumerating them. The selected independent-assortment/segment-exchange interpretation is an explicit biological inference, kept on the cytological/chromosomal level in the actual p87 introduction. The model context is supplied, not self-constructed.
bilingualFinding: DE/EN both require explanation from supplied meiosis-chromosome models and cover the same two routes to new genetic combinations. Neither requires a new model-construction algorithm.
understandingEvidence: Explain a new combination of already present information, distinguish whole-chromosome assortment and within-chromosome segment exchange, and distinguish both from a chromosome-number error.
performanceEvidence: Interpret two correctly supplied origin-marked chromosome comparisons, explain where the genetic combination changes and why the gametes remain complete haploid sets. Drawing or constructing models from memory is not required.
transferEvidence: Explain the same principle in another supplied correct model with different markers or origins; no fresh genetic-cross calculation or unsupported independent construction is added.
